\[
L = \text{sRGB}^{-1}\!\left(\frac{I}{255}\right),
\qquad
\text{out} = \left(\frac{T(L) - \min T}{\max T - \min T}\right)^{1/\gamma}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(L\): Linear light from 0 to 1
- \(T\): The tone mapping operator
- \(\gamma\): The display gamma

The 8-bit values are decoded to linear light L, since the operators expect radiance. T is the chosen operator. Reinhard and Devlin map each value with a photoreceptor curve I / (I + (f I_a)^m). The adaptation level I_a mixes the pixel, its channel and the image mean. Drago et al. take a logarithm whose base changes with brightness. The bias sets how. Mantiuk et al. turn the log luminance into a pyramid of gradients, multiply the contrast response by the scale, and rebuild the image. OpenCV then stretches T from its minimum to its maximum and applies 1 / gamma.
